svg.title: The lethal trifecta as three overlapping sets
svg.desc: Three equal circles overlap in the classic three-set arrangement, their centres one radius apart. The upper circle is numbered one, access to private data, the model can read it. The lower left is numbered two, untrusted content, anyone can write it. The lower right is numbered three, an outbound channel, a write or a fetch. Only the region where all three overlap is marked: it is hatched in red and its three arcs are traced in a heavier red stroke, and it is labelled exfiltration is possible. A leader line runs from it up to a note saying an attacker who can write into two can make the model read one and send it out through three. A second note says that removing any one circle closes the path, and that no amount of filtering closes it while all three remain. Three cards along the bottom give one example of each property from this series' own projects: the database analyst, which holds a select grant on the customer tables; the research browser, which fetches arbitrary pages that strangers wrote; and the devops responder, which can patch a live cluster and reach the network.
svg.text: Willison, 2025. Each property alone is ordinary. Only the middle is an exfiltration path.
